questions.question: The 11th Fundamental Duty provides opportunities for education for the ______ age group of children.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6-14 years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty was added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002.
 
• It states that it is the duty of every parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to their child or ward between the **ages of 6 and 14 years**.
 
• This amendment also led to the insertion of Article 21A, making education a fundamental right for children in this age group.
 
• It emphasizes the importance of education in the development and empowerment of children, ensuring their right to free and compulsory education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Constitution (Eighty-Sixth Amendment) Act, 2002, was enacted to provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of six to fourteen years as a fundamental right.
 
• Article 51A (k) was added to the Constitution under Part IV-A (Fundamental Duties), which specifies this duty of parents and guardians.
 
• Education is a critical factor in the growth and development of an individual and the nation.
 
• The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, commonly known as the RTE Act, was enacted to implement this constitutional provision.

questions.question: Article 356 and 360 in the Indian constitution are the articles based on ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**emergency provisions.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 356** is related to the** imposition of President's Rule** in a state, which is a form of** emergency provision** used when the state government is unable to function properly.
 
• **Article 360** deals with the** financial emergency** that can be imposed in the country when the financial stability or credit of India is threatened.
 
• The emergency provisions in the Indian constitution are of three types -** national emergency, state emergency, and financial emergency.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Regional languages** are not directly related to either Article 356 or 360, although language can be a factor in the** imposition of President's Rule** in a state.
 
• **Amendment of the constitution** is not related to these articles, as it is covered under a separate set of articles in the constitution.

questions.question: The legislative powers in India are divided into three lists, which are the Union List, the State List and the __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Concurrent List**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Concurrent List includes subjects of common interest to both the Union and State governments.
 
• It is enumerated in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Both the Parliament and State Legislatures can make laws on the subjects in the Concurrent List.
 
• In case of conflict between the Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include criminal law, marriage and divorce, bankruptcy and insolvency, and education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List:** Contains subjects of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways. Only the Parliament can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **State List:** Contains subjects of local or state importance like police, public health, agriculture, and fisheries. Only the State Legislatures can legislate on these subjects.
 
• **Federal Structure:** India follows a quasi-federal structure, where powers are divided between the central and state governments, with a strong centralizing bias.
 
• **Seventh Schedule:** The division of powers between the Union and State governments is outlined in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, which contains the Union List, State List, and Concurrent List.
 
• **Residual Powers:** Any subject not mentioned in any of the three lists falls under the residuary powers, which are vested in the Parliament.

questions.question: Which of the following fundamental duties was added to the Indian Constitution by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002?

options.text: To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem
To protect and to improve the natural environment including forests, lakes, rivers and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures
To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years
To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide opportunities for education to his/her child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002**, added the fundamental duty of providing opportunities for education to children between the ages of six and fourteen years.
 
• This amendment also led to the insertion of **Article 21A **in the Constitution, making education a fundamental right for children in this age group.
 
• The amendment emphasizes the role of parents and guardians in ensuring that children receive the necessary education.
 
• This duty reflects the importance placed on education as a means of individual and societal development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The** fundamental duties** are enshrined in** Part IV-A **of the Constitution of India, under Article 51A.
 
• Originally, ten fundamental duties were listed, but the 86th Amendment Act added an eleventh duty.
 
• The concept of fundamental duties was borrowed from the Constitution of the former Soviet Union and was added to the Indian Constitution by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens to respect the ideals and institutions of the nation.
 
• While these duties are non-justiciable, they are considered essential for the overall development and unity of the country.

questions.question: From which of the following countries has the Indian Constitution borrowed the concept of the Concurrent List?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of Australia.
 
• The Concurrent List allows both the Union and the State Governments to legislate on certain matters.
 
• This list includes subjects like marriage, bankruptcy, trade unions, and education.
 
• In case of a conflict between Union and State laws on a concurrent subject, the law made by the Union Government prevails.
 
• The inclusion of the Concurrent List ensures a balance of power and responsibilities between the central and state governments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Union List**

 
 
• The Union List consists of subjects on which only the central government can legislate.
 
• It includes matters of national importance like defense, foreign affairs, atomic energy, and railways.
 
• There are 97 subjects listed under the Union List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **State List**
 
 
• The State List comprises subjects on which only the state governments can legislate.
 
• It includes matters of local or state importance such as police, public health, and agriculture.
 
• There are 66 subjects listed under the State List in the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Seventh Schedule**
 
 
• The Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution outlines the division of powers between the Union and State governments.
 
• It contains three lists: the Union List, the State List, and the Concurrent List.
 
• This schedule is crucial for maintaining the federal structure of India.
 
 
 
• **Residual Powers**
 
 
• Residual powers refer to subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists.
 
• According to the Indian Constitution, residual powers rest with the Union Government.
 
• This provision ensures that any new subject of legislation that arises is dealt with at the national level.

questions.question: Which of the following articles of the Indian constitution provides for National commission for Scheduled Castes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 338**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The correct answer is option 4, i.e. Article 338 of the Indian Constitution provides for the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.**
 
• This article was inserted by the** 65th Amendment Act of 1990.**
 
• The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is a constitutional body that is responsible for safeguarding the rights and interests of the scheduled castes and monitoring the implementation of constitutional safeguards for them.
 
• The Commission investigates and monitors all matters relating to the constitutional and other legal safeguards for the protection of the rights and interests of the scheduled castes and submits reports to the President and the Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Article 337**: This article deals with the appointment of a special officer for linguistic minorities.
 
• **Article 344**: This article deals with the appointment of a Commission to examine the conditions of backward classes.
 
• ** Article 343: **This article deals with the official language of the Union.

questions.question: In the Indian constitution, the Right to Freedom is covered from ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Article 19 to 22**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The right to freedom gives citizens basic freedom with respect to speech and expression, form associations, freedom of personal liberty, freedom to live a life of dignity, etc.
 
• It is important to understand the scope of these provisions and any exceptions thereof.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** The fundamental rights were originally provided by the Constitution 

 
• Right to equality (Article 14–18)
 
• Right to freedom (Article 19–22)
 
• Right against exploitation (Article 23–24)
 
• Right to freedom of religion (Article 25–28)
 
• Cultural and educational rights (Article 29–30)
 
• Right to constitutional remedies (Article 32)
 
• Right to Education (Article 21A)

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) 2005 provides _______ days of assured employment every year to every rural household.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**100**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) provide 100 days of guaranteed wage employment.
 
• This was initiated with the objective of “enhancing livelihood security in rural areas by providing at least 100 days of guaranteed wage employment in a financial year, especially to households whose adult members volunteer to do unskilled manual work".
 
• This Act also aims to create durable assets (such as roads, canals, ponds, and wells).
 
• Within 5 km of an applicant’s residence, employment is provided.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objectives of MGNREGA:**

 
 
• The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) 
 
• Provide 100 days of guaranteed wage employment to rural unskilled labour
 
• Increase economic security.
 
• Decrease migration of labour from rural to urban areas.
 
• It was known to be the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act.
 
• MGNREGA Job Card is a document that renders a worker entitled to work under the MGNREGA scheme.

questions.question: Part XVI of the Indian constitution deals with _____

options.text: Special provisions related to certain classes
Special provisions related to municipal corporation

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Special provisions related to certain classes.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Part XVI** of the Indian Constitution deals with **special provisions** related to certain classes.
 
• This part includes provisions for the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, and Other Backward Classes (OBCs) to ensure their social and economic welfare.
 
• The provisions include reservations in** education, employment, and political representation.**
 
• These special provisions aim to **uplift the marginalized sections of society** and provide them with equal opportunities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Elections **are covered under **Part XV **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Constitutional amendments** are covered under **Part XX **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• **Special provisions** related to municipal corporations are covered under **Part IXA of the Indian Constitution.**

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** ****__Right to Equality__.**

• The Constitution provided for Six Fundamental Rights,
 
• Right to equality comprises Articles 14-18 they are, 
 
• Equality before the law and equal protection of laws **(Article 14).**
 
• Article 15 of the constitution deals with the Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth which is under the right to equality
